title: Tata Motors plans local assembly of Iveco vehicles, eyes global expansion
description:
Tata Motors and Italy-headquartered Iveco on Tuesday announced that the combined enterprise will be the world's fourth-largest commercial vehicle maker with a revenue of Rs 2.28 lakh crore (Euro 21 billion).
The Indian auto major acquired an 89.42 per cent stake in Iveco for nearly 3.43 billion euros post the initial settlement of its cash tender offer, even as the buyout continues.
The acquisition of Iveco, making it an indirect subsidiary of the Indian auto major, will be Tata Motors' biggest since it bought Jaguar Land Rover from Ford in 2008. Iveco Group employs 33,000 people and operates 16 industrial sites and 22 R&D centres.
The settlement follows the completion of the acceptance period of the voluntary tender offer, under which Tata Motors offered EUR 14.4 per share in cash for Iveco's common shares.
